explanation: One of the patriarchs in the Bible, son of Isaac and Rebekah, and father of the twelve tribes of Israel.
Jacob's older twin brother, whom Jacob deceived for both the birthright and the blessing from their father Isaac.
Spiritual beings who serve God and carry out his will; in this context, Jacob meets a group of angels.
The place where Jacob sets up camp after crossing the Jabbok River and sending his servants, family, and possessions across the river.
A tributary of the Jordan River, which Jacob crosses before meeting Esau again after many years.
A divine gift or favor that may include protection, prosperity, fertility, or other benefits.
Jacob wrestles with a man (assumed to be an angel or God himself) through the night and is blessed by him.
The name given to Jacob after his struggle, meaning "God struggles" or "he who struggles with God".
